title: Sheaf tensor with an ideal quotient, normalized on sections and quotient maps
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal subsheaf (a subsheaf stable under multiplication by local sections of $R$). For an $R$-module sheaf $F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $IF\subseteq F$ be the subsheaf whose sections are locally finite sums $\sum_a i_af_a$, with $i_a\in I$ and $f_a\in F$ on the members of a covering sieve. Put $S=R/I$ and $Q_I(F)=F/IF$, with quotients formed by sheafifying the sectionwise quotients [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Use sheaf tensor and its pure sections [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. Then $Q_I(F)$ has its canonical $S$-module structure, and there is an $S$-linear isomorphism
$$a_{I,F}:F\otimes_R S\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_I(F),\qquad f\otimes\bar r\longmapsto[rf],\qquad a_{I,F}^{-1}([f])=f\otimes1.$$
These formulas mean identities on images of local sections in the sheafifications. Writing $q_{I,F}:F\to Q_I(F)$ and $u_{I,F}:F\to F\otimes_RS$ for $f\mapsto[f]$ and $f\mapsto f\otimes1$, one has $a_{I,F}u_{I,F}=q_{I,F}$; in particular $u_{I,F}$ is an epimorphism with kernel $IF$. For any $R$-linear sheaf morphism $h:F\to G$, the induced quotient map $Q_I(h)([f])=[h(f)]$ satisfies
$$Q_I(h)a_{I,F}=a_{I,G}(h\otimes1).$$
For any ideal subsheaf $I'\subseteq I$, let $t:R/I'\to R/I$ and $v:Q_{I'}(F)\to Q_I(F)$ be the quotient maps. After restriction to $R$-modules,
$$v\,a_{I',F}=a_{I,F}(1_F\otimes t),\qquad (1_F\otimes t)u_{I',F}=u_{I,F}.$$
No flatness of $F$, existence of points, or surjectivity of $R(U)\to S(U)$ on every object is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafification of the tensor-quotient balanced maps; the quotient identification and its two naturality squares are the agent-written extraction of the original item steps 2–5.

proof.text: Work in a common value universe containing the small site, so the local-section theorem applies. Module sheafification has underlying abelian sheaf the abelian-group sheafification, and abelian-group and commutative-ring sheafification commute with underlying sets. Apply the cited local-section theorem to these underlying presheaves. Consequently every section of $S=(U\mapsto R(U)/I(U))^\#$ is locally the image of a class $\bar r$, hence locally of an $r\in R$; equality of two such images means their representatives differ by a section of $I$ after a covering refinement. Likewise, sections of a sheafified module quotient are locally represented by module elements, and equality of their images is equality in the quotient presheaf after refinement. All local arguments below use covering sieves and their pullbacks along arrows; comparisons are on common restriction cones, so the site need not have fibre products.

source.place: Tags 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures) and 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification); module identification from Tag 03CY

proof.text: The locally finite-sum prescription for $IF$ is closed under restriction, addition, negatives and multiplication by $R$: refine the two covering sieves and combine their finite sums, or multiply each summand. If sections of $IF$ glue in $F$, their local finite-sum witnesses compose with the gluing cover, so the glued section again belongs to $IF$. Thus $IF$ is an $R$-submodule sheaf. Set $P(U)=F(U)/IF(U)$ and $Q=P^\#$. The local equality criterion of step 1 gives $q(f)=0$ exactly when $f$ belongs to $IF$ locally, which is equivalent to $f\in IF(U)$ by this subsheaf property. Hence $\ker q=IF$. To check that $q$ is epic, let two morphisms out of $Q$ agree after $q$. Every section of $Q$ is locally $q(f)$ by step 1, so their values agree locally, and separatedness of the target gives equality. This proves right cancellation for $q$, without sectionwise surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), applied to the sheafified module quotient; local ideal-product argument written out here

proof.text: Put $S_0(U)=R(U)/I(U)$. The presheaf $P$ of step 2 is an $S_0$-module by $\bar r[f]=[rf]$: replacing $r$ by $r+i$ changes $rf$ by $if\in IF(U)$, and replacing $f$ by $f+x$, $x\in IF(U)$, changes $rf$ by $rx\in IF(U)$. Additivity, the unit, associativity and compatibility with restrictions are the corresponding identities in $F$. Apply the cited module-sheafification interface with coefficient presheaf $S_0$, its ring sheafification $S$, and module presheaf $P$. It equips the same underlying abelian sheaf $P^\#=Q$ with the canonical $S$-action extending $\bar r[f]=[rf]$. Its restricted $R$-action agrees with the original action by uniqueness of the compatible sheafification action. This is the asserted canonical $S$-module structure.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), applied to the quotient ring presheaf and its module quotient

proof.text: Construct a pairing $B:F\times S\to Q$ as follows. For $f\in F(U)$ and $s\in S(U)$, choose local representatives $s|_V=\bar r_V$ as in step 1 and put $B(f,s)|_V=q(r_V f|_V)$. On any common restriction cone, two representatives of $s$ differ locally by $i\in I$, so the two proposed values differ by $q(if)=0$. Separatedness makes them agree on the cone, and the sheaf condition glues them uniquely. This also proves independence of the chosen cover and compatibility with restrictions. On a common refinement the identities for $B(f+g,s)$, $B(f,s+t)$, and $B(af,s)=B(f,as)$ reduce respectively to $(r(f+g)=rf+rg)$, $((r+r')f=rf+r'f)$, and $(raf=arf)$ in $F$; hence $B$ is $R$-bilinear. On each $U$ the defining relations of the module tensor therefore give a linear map $F(U)\otimes_{R(U)}S(U)\to Q(U)$ sending $f\otimes s$ to $B(f,s)$. These maps commute with restrictions. The module-sheafification universal property extends them uniquely to $a:F\otimes_R S\to Q$. In particular $a(f\otimes\bar r)=q(rf)$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor followed by sheafification; local representatives justified by the cited local-section theorem

proof.text: Define $u:F\to F\otimes_R S$ by $u(f)=f\otimes1$, using the pure-section map and its restriction compatibility. For $i\in I(U)$, balancing gives $u(if)=if\otimes1=f\otimes\bar i=0$. If $x\in IF(U)$, locally $x=\sum_a i_af_a$, so $u(x)$ is locally zero by additivity and this calculation; separatedness gives $u(x)=0$. Thus the section maps $[f]\mapsto f\otimes1$ are well-defined $R(U)$-linear maps $P(U)\to(F\otimes_R S)(U)$ compatible with restrictions. Sheafify them by the universal property to obtain $b:Q\to F\otimes_R S$ with $b(q(f))=u(f)$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product) and Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), tensor balancing and descent through the quotient presheaf

proof.text: On $f\in F(U)$ the composite $ab$ satisfies $ab(q(f))=a(f\otimes1)=q(f)$, so $ab=1_Q$ by the epimorphism $q$ proved in step 2. For the other composite, take a pure section $f\otimes s$ and restrict to a cover where $s=\bar r$. There $ba(f\otimes\bar r)=b(q(rf))=rf\otimes1=f\otimes\bar r$. Separatedness proves this equality for every pure section, and the pure-section extensionality gives $ba=1_{F\otimes_R S}$. For $S$-linearity of $a$, take $s,t\in S(U)$ and refine until $s=\bar r$, $t=\bar c$. Then $a(t(f\otimes s))=a(f\otimes\overline{cr})=q(crf)=tq(rf)=t\,a(f\otimes s)$. Local equality and tensor extensionality extend this to all sections. Thus $a$ is an $S$-linear isomorphism; its inverse $b$ is $S$-linear because applying the injective $a$ to $b(ty)$ and $t b(y)$ gives $ty$ in both cases. This proves both displayed formulas, including their meaning on images in sheafification.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), inverse and scalar-linearity calculations on pure sections

proof.text: The formula $a(u(f))=q(f)$ proves $au=q$ on all local sections, hence as sheaf morphisms. Since $a$ is invertible, right cancellation for $q$ implies right cancellation for $u$: if $c u=d u$, then $(c b)q=(d b)q$, so $c b=d b$ and $c=d$. Also $u(f)=0$ if and only if $q(f)=0$, which by step 2 holds if and only if $f\in IF(U)$. Consequently $u$ is epic and its kernel is precisely $IF$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), elementary consequences of the constructed inverse and the quotient kernel from step 2

proof.text: For an $R$-linear sheaf map $h:F\to G$, a local sum $\sum i_af_a$ maps to $\sum i_a h(f_a)$, so $h(IF)\subseteq IG$. It induces the presheaf maps $[f]\mapsto[h(f)]$, and sheafification gives $Q_I(h)$. The formula in step 3 shows it is $S$-linear on local representatives, hence everywhere. On a pure section with second factor locally $\bar r$, the two proposed composites are $Q_I(h)a_{I,F}(f\otimes\bar r)=[h(rf)]=[r h(f)]$ and $a_{I,G}(h(f)\otimes\bar r)=[r h(f)]$. Restricting to such covers, using separatedness, and then pure-section extensionality proves $Q_I(h)a_{I,F}=a_{I,G}(h\otimes1)$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), agent-written naturality calculation for module morphisms

proof.text: If $I'\subseteq I$, then $I'F\subseteq IF$ from the local finite-sum definition. The sectionwise quotient maps sheafify to $t:S'=R/I'\to S=R/I$ and $v:Q_{I'}(F)\to Q_I(F)$; they are $R$-linear. For a pure section in $F\otimes_R S'$, refine until its second factor is the image of some $r\in R$. The first composite gives $v a_{I',F}(f\otimes\bar r) = v([rf]_{I'})=[rf]_I$; the second gives $a_{I,F}(1\otimes t)(f\otimes\bar r)=a_{I,F}(f\otimes\bar r)=[rf]_I$. Local equality and pure-section extensionality give the first ideal-inclusion identity. Finally $(1\otimes t)u_{I',F}(f)=f\otimes t(1)=f\otimes1=u_{I,F}(f)$, proving the second. All these equations are taken after restriction to $R$-modules, as required.
